habit.lifeForm.basis: RHS record of the accepted name: a large, vigorous, deciduous climber "with twining stems".

stem.twiningHandedness.basis: As in taxon.json. RHS: Japanese wisterias "twine clockwise", no viewpoint stated; Bean: "its stems twining clockwise"; Japanese floras, as compiled on ja.wikipedia, give the viewpoint: clockwise seen from above, an S-twist. That is a left-handed helix (vocab.ts HANDEDNESS), the opposite of W. sinensis. One source read says the reverse in words (US Forest Service FEIS, after Miller 2006: Japanese wisteria anticlockwise); it gives no viewpoint and stands alone.

stem.youngSurface.basis: Compton and others (2019, PhytoKeys 125), description of the genus: stems round in section, green and downy when young. Japanese floras (ja.wikipedia) add short brown hairs on the young twig that are soon lost.

stem.matureColour.basis: Compton and others (2019), of the genus: stems grey or reddish brown when mature.

stem.oldBark.value: grey, smooth, dotted with lenticels; old trunks fluted and muscle-like
stem.oldBark.basis: NC State Extension: bark dark grey with white dots, old trunks fluted and muscle-like. The Seattle Japanese Garden says the same of its plants: smooth and grey, becoming "fluted and muscle-like". Japanese floras: greyish brown with many lenticels.

stem.oldDiameterM.basis: The upper figure: US Forest Service FEIS (after Swearingen and others 2002), old plants of W. floribunda and W. sinensis to 15 in. through. The lower: Japanese floras (ja.wikipedia, after Hotta 1989), stems reaching about 10 cm. Not drawn from: the thickness of a stem is the growth model's.

leaf.arrangement.basis: NC State Extension: leaves alternate, compound. The growth model's organs.leavesPerNode says the same: one leaf to a node.

leaf.division.basis: RHS record: leaves "divided into leaflets". University of Connecticut plant database: odd-pinnately compound, that is with an end leaflet.

leaf.lengthM.basis: Bean (Trees and Shrubs Online): "Leaves 10 to 15 in. long", the whole compound leaf, in metres. The growth model's organs.leafLengthM is the same figure.

leaf.leafletCount.basis: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria (HortFlora), of this cultivar: leaflets 11 to 17. Of the species Bean gives "usually eleven to nineteen", and the University of Connecticut 13 to 19.

leaf.leafletShape.basis: Bean: leaflets "of ovate shape". Kwantlen Polytechnic University plant database: mostly lanceolate-elliptic. Japanese floras: ovate-oblong to narrowly ovate.

leaf.leafletLengthM.basis: Japanese floras as compiled on ja.wikipedia (after Shinohara 2008): leaflets 4 to 10 cm long. The compilation was read, not the floras. Bean gives less, 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 in. (38 to 64 mm); Kwantlen 6 to 8 cm.

leaf.leafletWidthM.basis: Japanese floras as compiled on ja.wikipedia (after Tsujii 1995): leaflets about 2 to 2.5 cm wide. From the same compilation as the length, so that the two give a proportion: about three times as long as wide.

leaf.leafletTip.basis: Compton and others (2019), of the genus: leaflet tip acute, acuminate or drawn out into a short tail. Japanese floras: the tip drawn out.

leaf.leafletBase.basis: Japanese floras as compiled on ja.wikipedia: the base of the leaflet nearly round. Compton and others (2019), of the genus: base obtuse or cuneate.

leaf.leafletMargin.basis: Kwantlen Polytechnic University plant database: margin entire, the edges undulate. Compton and others (2019), of the genus: entire or gently wavy.

leaf.surface.value: glossy above, downy when young and soon smooth
leaf.surface.basis: Bean: leaflets "downy when young", soon nearly or quite smooth, and "a glossy dark green".

leaf.colour.basis: RHS record: "dark green leaves". Bean has them glossy and dark green.

leaf.youngColour.basis: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria (HortFlora), of this cultivar: leaflets "pale bronze when young".

leaf.autumnColour.basis: RHS record: leaves "that turn yellow in autumn".

inflorescence.type.basis: RHS record: "drooping racemes to 1m or more in length".

inflorescence.held.basis: RHS record: "drooping racemes". The growth model's names section records the same thing as flowerHeld: hanging.

inflorescence.position.value: at the end of short leafy shoots
inflorescence.position.basis: Bean: "Racemes borne on short leafy shoots". In the growth model these are the spurs, each with its few leaves and a raceme at its end.

inflorescence.lengthM.basis: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria (HortFlora), of this cultivar: flower clusters 0.5 to 1 m long, "occasionally more", the length varying with season and place. RHS record: to 1 m or more; RHS growing guide, of f. multijuga: up to 1.2 m. The growth model's organs.racemeLengthM (0.6 to 1.1 m) is chosen among these and says how.

inflorescence.lengthSpeciesM.basis: Compton and others (2019), key to the species of Wisteria: W. floribunda, inflorescence 18 to 120 cm long, against 12 to 20 cm in W. sinensis. Bean gives the wild plant 5 to 10 in.

inflorescence.lengthMeasure.value: the whole raceme, from where it leaves the shoot to its tip
inflorescence.lengthMeasure.basis: What organs.racemeLengthM in the growth model, and so RenderFlower.lengthM, measures for this taxon: the length of the raceme, as the floras give it. The viewer's raceme is authored to that measure, at the middle of the growth model's range.

inflorescence.widthM.basis: US Forest Service FEIS, of W. floribunda and W. sinensis together and without a citation of its own: racemes 3 to 4 in. (7 to 10 cm) wide. Not drawn from directly: the width of the drawn raceme follows from the flower stalk and the flower.

inflorescence.flowerCountSpecies.basis: Japanese floras as compiled on ja.wikipedia (after Hirano 1997): one raceme of the species can carry over 100 flowers. Entered as that floor; the compilation was read, not the book.

inflorescence.flowerCount.basis: No count of the flowers on a raceme of this cultivar was found. Chosen from what is recorded round it: the species carries over 100 on racemes mostly of 20 to 50 cm, a flower to 5 mm of stalk or less; this cultivar's flowers are "widely spaced along the stem" (Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria). 150 on a raceme of 0.85 m is one flower to rather under 6 mm, a little wider apart than the species. A count on a real raceme would settle it.

inflorescence.flowerSpacing.basis: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria (HortFlora), of this cultivar: the individual flowers "widely spaced along the stem".

inflorescence.openingOrder.value: successively from the base to the tip
inflorescence.openingOrder.basis: Bean: "the flowers opening successively from the base". The base is the top of a hanging raceme, so a raceme in mid-flower is open above and in bud below. Ohio State University: over several days, where W. sinensis opens almost all at once.

flower.shape.basis: RHS record: "fragrant, pea-like" flowers. A standard, two wings and a keel of two joined petals.

flower.standardColour.value: pale violet, with a yellow mark at its base
flower.standardColour.basis: Bean, of 'Multijuga': standard pale violet with a yellow mark at the base. Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria, of 'Macrobotrys': pale violet with a yellow blotch. Chris Lane (The Garden, May 2019), of 'Kyushaku': white flushed mauve, with a small yellow eye.

flower.wingAndKeelColour.basis: Bean, of 'Multijuga': wings and keel violet-blue. Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria: wings and keel a darker tone than the standard. Chris Lane, of 'Kyushaku': mauvish violet.

flower.standardWidthM.basis: The sources differ, and the span of the three is entered. Bean: "standard petal 3/4 in. wide" (19 mm), the widest. Compton and others (2019, key to the species): standard broadly ovate, 8 to 16 by 8 to 12 mm, against 20 to 30 mm each way in W. sinensis. Japanese floras (ja.wikipedia): nearly round, 10 to 13 mm across. The drawing takes the middle of the span, which makes the standard a little wider than long.

flower.standardLengthM.basis: Compton and others (2019), key to the species: standard 8 to 16 mm long. It is bent back near its base, so that it stands up from the flower.

flower.wingLengthM.basis: Japanese floras as compiled on ja.wikipedia (after Omiya 1997): wings and keel each about 15 to 20 mm long. Compton and others (2019), of the genus: wings 12 to 20 by 5 to 8 mm, keel 11 to 18 by 4 to 8 mm.

flower.wingWidthM.basis: Compton and others (2019), of the genus: wing petals 12 to 20 by 5 to 8 mm, as long as the keel or a little longer.

flower.keelLengthM.basis: Compton and others (2019), of the genus: keel petals 11 to 18 by 4 to 8 mm, joined into a blunt cup.

flower.calyxWidthM.basis: Compton and others (2019), of the genus: calyx 4 to 10 by 4 to 6 mm.

flower.stalkLengthM.basis: Bean: each flower "on a slightly downy stalk 1/2 to 1 in. long", in metres. Japanese floras: 15 to 25 mm.

flower.calyxLengthM.basis: Compton and others (2019), of the genus: calyx 4 to 10 by 4 to 6 mm, bell-shaped or tubular, five-toothed. Bean, of this species: "calyx 1/3 in. long, bell-shaped, with triangular teeth".

flower.stamenCount.basis: Compton and others (2019), of the genus: nine stamens joined and the tenth free. They lie inside the keel and are not drawn.

flower.opensRelativeToLeaves.basis: RHS growing guide: Japanese wisteria "bears flowers and leaves at the same time", where W. sinensis flowers before its leaves.

fruit.type.basis: RHS record: flowers "often followed by bean-like velvety, blue-grey seed pods".

fruit.lengthM.basis: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria (HortFlora), of this cultivar: pods 11 to 20 cm long. The growth model's fruit.lengthM is the same figure. Bean gives the species 3 to 6 in.

fruit.widthM.basis: Compton and others (2019), of the genus: pods 10 to 24 by 1.2 to 3 cm. Japanese floras, of this species: 2 to 2.5 cm wide, widest above the middle.

fruit.shape.value: flattened, widest towards the end, a little narrowed between the seeds
fruit.shape.basis: Compton and others (2019), of the genus: pods flattened and slightly narrowed between the seeds. Japanese floras, of this species: narrowly obovate and flat.

fruit.surface.basis: Bean: "Pods 3 to 6 in. long, velvety". Compton and others (2019): densely velvety.

fruit.colourUnripe.basis: RHS record: "velvety, blue-grey seed pods". Kwantlen Polytechnic University: green, maturing to brown.

fruit.colourRipe.basis: University of Connecticut plant database: brown pods, turning brown in October and staying on the plant. NC State Extension: brown to copper.

fruit.seedCount.basis: Compton and others (2019), of the genus: seeds usually 3 to 6 (1 to 8), lens-shaped, 8 to 12 mm across.

fruit.held.basis: RHS growing guide: established wisterias can form "pendant, bean-like seedpods".
